extraction.name: Science Question Answering (ScienceQA)
extraction.description: A new benchmark that consists of 21,208 multimodal multiple choice questions with diverse science topics and annotations of their answers with corresponding lectures and explanations. The dataset covers three subjects: natural science, social science, and language science, spanning grades 1-12.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan. Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. NeurIPS 2022.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in the SCIENCEQA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. The original science problems were downloaded and then individual components (e.g. questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted based on heuristic rules.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Individual components (e.g. questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted from original science problems based on heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed, such as questions that have only one choice, questions that contain faulty data, and questions that are duplicated. If there were multiple correct answers that applied, only one correct answer was kept. Answer options of each question were shuffled to ensure the choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat the lectures and solutions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid questions were manually removed, such as questions that have only one choice, questions that contain faulty data, and questions that are duplicated. If there were multiple correct answers that applied, only one correct answer was kept. Answer options of each question were shuffled to ensure the choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat the lectures and solutions. Special structures in the texts, such as tables and lists, are easily distinguishable from simple text passages. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples in the collected dataset, and incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions (83.9%) are annotated with lectures that provide general external knowledge introducing the background information for solving problems of a similar class. 90.5% of questions feature explanations that reveal specific reasons for the answer. Annotations were reviewed using a data exploration tool, and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 was used to extract captions from images as visual context.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not contain any user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCIENCEQA dataset collects science questions sourced from textbooks and is proposed to diagnose the multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. SCIENCEQA will contribute to the development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. After careful examination, no improper content such as pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias was found.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current multimodal methods fail to achieve satisfactory performance on SCIENCEQA and do not generate correct explanations. Language models still fail to answer a wide range of challenging questions. Failure cases can be classified into two types: (a) the model fails to understand the multimodal inputs and lacks domain-specific knowledge to arrive at the correct answer; (b) the model generates the wrong chain of thought with irrelevant, incorrect, or incomplete information. Image captions lack fine-grained semantics and usually do not work well for diagrams. Large language models face challenges in reasoning about questions that require understanding complex and uncommon domain knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for training, testing, and validation of models for multimodal question answering and multi-hop reasoning. SCIENCEQA provides a useful benchmark for multi-modal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence. The dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes only.
